overview.description: Skwitz is a nineteenth-century Austrian fishing card game for two to eight players, resembling Cassino.

history.origins: Skwitz is documented as a distinct traditional card game with its own player count, equipment, and objective.
timeline: Documented source page identifies Skwitz as a standalone game rather than only a synonym or expansion.

setup.players: 2-8 players use the table arrangement described for Skwitz.
setup.equipment: French-suited playing cards, score area, and enough table space for play.
setup.dealing: Prepare French-suited playing cards and deal or lay out cards according to the documented Skwitz rules before play begins.

rules.objective: Capture table cards and score according to the fishing-game rules.
rules.gameplay: Players play cards from hand to capture matching or combinable cards from the table, following a Cassino-like fishing structure. Captured cards are scored at the end of the hand.
keyRules: Fishing-type game for two to eight players.
Recorded in Austrian game compendia in the nineteenth century.

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck comprising four suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades. Each suit contains thirteen ranks: Ace, 2 through 10, Jack, Queen, and King, providing versatile options for various card games.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card iconography and distinct color coding for easy identification.
